headlines.title: Heavy rain and thunderstorms to bring flooding risk to the Bay Area Thursday
headlines.description: Downtown San Francisco on Wednesday set a new daily rainfall record for Nov. 18. As of 3 p.m., downtown had received 2.28 inches of rain, besting the old Nov. 18 record of 2.24 inches set way back in 1918, according to the National Weather Service. The rainiest day ever recorded in downtown San Francisco happened back on Nov. 5, 1994, when 5.54 inches of rain fell, according to the National Weather Service. bay area weather 20 hours ago power outages 19 hours ago bay area weather Nov 17 The day of torrential rain left homes, businesses, and roads in the city flooded. In SOMA, some streets looked more like lakes. Along Folsom Street, water inundated garages and homes. With more rain in the forecast this week and throughout this season, city leaders urged residents to expect that Wednesday’s flooding won’t be a one-time occurrence. “If your street saw flooding, I would urge you to keep your car away from the area going forward, when rain is coming again,” said San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie at a press conference Wednesday. After seeing what the storm did to their neighborhoods, some San Francisco residents lined up Wednesday night to pick up free sandbags from the city’s Department of Public Works in the Marina. “It’s better to have the sandbags and not need them, than need the sandbags and not have them,” said Marina resident Patrick Thomasma as he picked up ten sandbags to set up outside his home. San Francisco resident Kobe Wang also picked up sandbags Wednesday night, noting that water pooled outside his house Wednesday, flooding his roommate’s car. Now, Wang is making plans for where to position the sandbags to better protect the home. Wang said he’d put the sandbags at the garage and in front of the door, noting the home has rooms in the basement.
